title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed steps for connecting and adjusting the pitch trim servo control cable during installation to ensure proper tension and alignment?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of magnetic devices during bonding process may lead to scratching on the landing gear strut. Only use OEM instructions and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

Remove the Pitch Trim Servo . (1)  Make sure the MASTER and AVIONICS switches are in the off position. (2)  Remove the access panels . Refer to Chapter 6, Access/Inspection Plates - Description and Operation. (3) Disconnect the electrical connector  from the pitch trim servo. (4)  Release the control cable tension and loosen the pitch trim servo control cable at the turnbuckle. (5)  Remove the bolts and washers that attach the pitch trim servo to the bracket assembly. (6)  Remove the pitch trim servo from the airplane. (7) Do an inspection of the pitch trim servo. Refer to Pitch Trim Servo Inspection.Install the Pitch Trim Servo . (1) Put the pitch trim servo in position on the bracket assembly and attach with the bolts and washers. (2) Connect the electrical connector  to the pitch trim servo. (3) Do the pitch trim servo control cable rigging. (a) The servo trim chain must be on the aft sprocket of the actuator before the manual trim system rigging can be done. (b) You must do the manual trim system rigging before the servo trim system rigging. Refer to Chapter 27, Elevator Trim Control - Maintenance Practices, Trim Tab Control Adjustment! Test. (c)  Put the elevator in the neutral position. (d) Use an inclinometer to put the trim tab to 5 degrees up in relation to the elevator. NOTE:  The chain sprocket on the actuator will be at approximately the halfway point in its rotation from the mechanical stops. (e) Move the servo trim chain on the aft sprocket of the actuator so that equal lengths of the chain are on either side of the sprocket. (f)  Wind the control cable around the pitch trim servo drum approximately 1 .25 turns each direction from the swaged ball. (g) Make sure the flanges of the control cable guard do not touch the control cable. (h) Make sure the flanges of the control cable guard are on either side of the notches around the outer edge of the mount. (i)  Use the turnbuckle to adjust the pitch trim servo control cable tension to 15 pounds, +3 or -3 pounds. (4) Install the access panels . Refer to Chapter 6, Access/inspection Plates - Description and Operation. (5) Put the MASTER and AVIONICS switches in the ON position. (6) Do a test of the autopilot to make sure it operates correctly. Refer to Introduction, the List of Manufacturers Technical Publications, for the manufacturer's installation manual.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the detailed procedure for verifying the pitch trim tab's travel limits and position with an inclinometer after manually operating the trim to full nose-up and observing clutch slip during rigging checks?
answer:
CAUTION: Before beginning any fastener removal, verify that the fuselage skin is isolated and secured. {Mistake} may result in unnecessary rework or component leakage.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What specific actions are performed to ensure the pitch trim system is properly rigged and functioning within its specified travel limits, including checks for control cable tension, clutch slip, and stop block positioning?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5)  Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9)  Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c) Repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What procedures are recommended for inspecting the pitch servo's electrical and mechanical components to ensure proper operation?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

question: What detailed steps are necessary to verify the proper operation and correct rigging of the pitch trim system, including checking the trim tab's travel limits, clutch slip, control cable tension, and stop block positioning?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5)  Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9)  Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot. Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c) Repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What procedures should be followed to verify that the pitch trim tab remains within its travel limits and to detect any slipping of the stop blocks during the rigging process?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: What specific precautions should be taken to prevent damage and ensure safety during the disassembly and inspection of the pitch servo's cover, solenoid, clutch, and motor?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What detailed steps are necessary to verify the correct operation of the pitch trim system, including checking for stop block slippage and ensuring the trim tab remains within specified travel limits?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the process for verifying that the pitch trim system's travel limits are accurate and that the stop blocks have not slipped during the rigging procedure?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5)  Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c) Repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: What are the specific steps involved in setting the autopilot roll null during pre-flight testing to ensure proper servo drive voltage?
answer:
CAUTION: Do not use alternative materials or substitute parts during this panel replacement. Using unapproved approved parts may lead to respiratory issues and void the warranty.

Set the Autopilot Roll Null . (1) Make sure the autopilot flight computer completes the pre-flight test. (2) Disconnect the roll servo connector from the airplane harness. (3) Apply a ground to pin K of the harness connector. (4) Connect a digital multimeter across the harness connector at pins D and L to monitor the servo drive voltage. (5) Push the autopilot AP button on the autopilot flight computer to engage it. (a)  Make sure the default ROL mode is set. NOTE:  For example, the HDG, NAV or APR modes are not engaged. (b)  Use a DMVM to measure the DC voltage across pins D and L of the roll servo harness connector. (c) Adjust the pot until a value of 0 volts, +0.020 or -0.020 volts are measured. 1  If the end of the pot movement is reached before the servo drive is nulled, disengage the autopilot, turn the pot fully to the opposite stop and then engage the autopilot. (d) The roll null adjustment range emulates a four turn pot that lets the method of the pot adjustment range to be set. NOTE:  This adjustment lets offsets be in the roll axes.  This includes the turn coordinator. (e) Continue to turn the pot to null the voltage. (6) Connect the airplane roll servo harness connector to the servo connector.

question: What are the detailed steps and safety precautions involved in removing, inspecting, and reinstalling the pitch servo cover, solenoid, clutch, and motor to ensure proper operation and prevent electrostatic damage?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How can you determine if the pitch trim stop blocks have slipped during the rigging check?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What specific checks should be performed to verify the proper functioning of the pitch servo's clutch and motor during inspection?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What method is used to verify that the pitch trim tab does not exceed its travel limits and that the stop blocks are properly engaged?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: What are the detailed procedures for verifying proper control cable tension and alignment after reinstalling the pitch trim servo?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of magnetic devices during bonding process may lead to scratching on the landing gear strut. Only use OEM instructions and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

Remove the Pitch Trim Servo . (1)  Make sure the MASTER and AVIONICS switches are in the off position. (2)  Remove the access panels . Refer to Chapter 6, Access/Inspection Plates - Description and Operation. (3) Disconnect the electrical connector  from the pitch trim servo. (4)  Release the control cable tension and loosen the pitch trim servo control cable at the turnbuckle. (5)  Remove the bolts and washers that attach the pitch trim servo to the bracket assembly. (6)  Remove the pitch trim servo from the airplane. (7) Do an inspection of the pitch trim servo. Refer to Pitch Trim Servo Inspection.Install the Pitch Trim Servo . (1) Put the pitch trim servo in position on the bracket assembly and attach with the bolts and washers. (2) Connect the electrical connector  to the pitch trim servo. (3) Do the pitch trim servo control cable rigging. (a) The servo trim chain must be on the aft sprocket of the actuator before the manual trim system rigging can be done. (b) You must do the manual trim system rigging before the servo trim system rigging. Refer to Chapter 27, Elevator Trim Control - Maintenance Practices, Trim Tab Control Adjustment! Test. (c)  Put the elevator in the neutral position. (d) Use an inclinometer to put the trim tab to 5 degrees up in relation to the elevator. NOTE:  The chain sprocket on the actuator will be at approximately the halfway point in its rotation from the mechanical stops. (e) Move the servo trim chain on the aft sprocket of the actuator so that equal lengths of the chain are on either side of the sprocket. (f)  Wind the control cable around the pitch trim servo drum approximately 1 .25 turns each direction from the swaged ball. (g) Make sure the flanges of the control cable guard do not touch the control cable. (h) Make sure the flanges of the control cable guard are on either side of the notches around the outer edge of the mount. (i)  Use the turnbuckle to adjust the pitch trim servo control cable tension to 15 pounds, +3 or -3 pounds. (4) Install the access panels . Refer to Chapter 6, Access/inspection Plates - Description and Operation. (5) Put the MASTER and AVIONICS switches in the ON position. (6) Do a test of the autopilot to make sure it operates correctly. Refer to Introduction, the List of Manufacturers Technical Publications, for the manufacturer's installation manual.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the specific safety measures and inspection procedures to verify the proper functioning of the pitch servo's cover, wiring, solenoid, clutch, and motor?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What specific procedures should be followed to manually operate and verify the pitch trim tab's travel limits, clutch slip, and control cable tension during rigging, and how can potential issues such as stop block slippage be identified and corrected?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5)  Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9)  Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c) Repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: How can the position of the pitch trim tab be checked to ensure it remains within specified travel limits and to detect if the stop blocks have slipped?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5)  Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c) Repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

question: What actions should be performed to verify the correct operation and travel limits of the pitch trim system, including checking for stop block slippage?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: What detailed steps are necessary to confirm that the pitch trim system's travel limits are correctly set and that the stop blocks have not slipped during the rigging process?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed procedures for inspecting the pitch servo's solenoid, clutch, and motor to confirm their proper operation and safety?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the recommended safety precautions and detailed steps for inspecting the pitch servo's cover, wiring, solenoid, clutch, and motor to ensure proper operation and prevent electrostatic damage?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed steps involved in inspecting and adjusting the pitch trim rigging to ensure the trim tab operates within its specified travel limits and to identify potential issues such as stop block slippage or control cable misadjustment?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5)  Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9)  Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c) Repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the recommended procedures for inspecting the pitch servo's solenoid, clutch, and motor to ensure their proper functionality and safety?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

answer:

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. question: What are the detailed steps involved in adjusting the autopilot roll null to ensure the servo drive voltage is properly nulled during the ground test?
answer:
CAUTION: Do not use alternative materials or substitute parts during this panel replacement. Using unapproved approved parts may lead to respiratory issues and void the warranty.

Set the Autopilot Roll Null . (1) Make sure the autopilot flight computer completes the pre-flight test. (2) Disconnect the roll servo connector from the airplane harness. (3) Apply a ground to pin K of the harness connector. (4) Connect a digital multimeter across the harness connector at pins D and L to monitor the servo drive voltage. (5) Push the autopilot AP button on the autopilot flight computer to engage it. (a)  Make sure the default ROL mode is set. NOTE:  For example, the HDG, NAV or APR modes are not engaged. (b)  Use a DMVM to measure the DC voltage across pins D and L of the roll servo harness connector. (c) Adjust the pot until a value of 0 volts, +0.020 or -0.020 volts are measured. 1  If the end of the pot movement is reached before the servo drive is nulled, disengage the autopilot, turn the pot fully to the opposite stop and then engage the autopilot. (d) The roll null adjustment range emulates a four turn pot that lets the method of the pot adjustment range to be set. NOTE:  This adjustment lets offsets be in the roll axes.  This includes the turn coordinator. (e) Continue to turn the pot to null the voltage. (6) Connect the airplane roll servo harness connector to the servo connector.

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What detailed steps are involved in performing a comprehensive check of the pitch trim rigging, including verifying the trim tab travel limits, clutch slip, control cable tension, and stop block positioning to ensure proper operation and identify potential issues?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5)  Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9)  Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c) Repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and repeat the check of the pitch trim rigging.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: What steps are taken to verify the correct operation and travel limits of the pitch trim tab during rigging inspection?
answer:
CAUTION: Before beginning any fastener removal, verify that the fuselage skin is isolated and secured. {Mistake} may result in unnecessary rework or component leakage.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.

question: What precautions should be observed to prevent electrostatic damage during the inspection of the pitch servo?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. Set the Autopilot Roll Null . (1) Make sure the autopilot flight computer completes the pre-flight test. (2) Disconnect the roll servo connector from the airplane harness. (5) Push the autopilot AP button on the autopilot flight computer to engage it. (a)  Make sure the default ROL mode is set. NOTE:  For example, the HDG, NAV or APR modes are not engaged. (d) The roll null adjustment range emulates a four turn pot that lets the method of the pot adjustment range to be set. NOTE:  This adjustment lets offsets be in the roll axes.  This includes the turn coordinator. (e) Continue to turn the pot to null the voltage. (6) Connect the airplane roll servo harness connector to the servo connector.

question: What steps should be taken to ensure safety and proper inspection when examining the pitch servo's solenoid, clutch, and motor?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the recommended steps to verify the proper functioning of the slip-clutch torque setting during roll servo inspection?
answer:
NOTE: This procedure applies specifically to aircraft models with engine nacelle configurations post-2015. For older models, refer to AMM revision 22B or later. Always verify aircraft model before beginning.

Do Inspection the Roll Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b) Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover over the wiring harness. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c) Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection of the roll servo. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4)  Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (5)  Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

title: AUTOPILOT - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How can you verify that the pitch trim tab's travel limits are correctly set and that the stop blocks have not slipped during the rigging process?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: What is the procedure for adjusting the autopilot roll null to achieve a voltage of approximately zero volts across the harness connector?
answer:
CAUTION: Do not use alternative materials or substitute parts during this panel replacement. Using unapproved approved parts may lead to respiratory issues and void the warranty.

Set the Autopilot Roll Null . (1) Make sure the autopilot flight computer completes the pre-flight test. (2) Disconnect the roll servo connector from the airplane harness. (3) Apply a ground to pin K of the harness connector. (4) Connect a digital multimeter across the harness connector at pins D and L to monitor the servo drive voltage. (5) Push the autopilot AP button on the autopilot flight computer to engage it. (a)  Make sure the default ROL mode is set. NOTE:  For example, the HDG, NAV or APR modes are not engaged. (b)  Use a DMVM to measure the DC voltage across pins D and L of the roll servo harness connector. (c) Adjust the pot until a value of 0 volts, +0.020 or -0.020 volts are measured. 1  If the end of the pot movement is reached before the servo drive is nulled, disengage the autopilot, turn the pot fully to the opposite stop and then engage the autopilot. (d) The roll null adjustment range emulates a four turn pot that lets the method of the pot adjustment range to be set. NOTE:  This adjustment lets offsets be in the roll axes.  This includes the turn coordinator. (e) Continue to turn the pot to null the voltage. (6) Connect the airplane roll servo harness connector to the servo connector.

question: What steps are involved in assessing the pitch trim system's travel limits and ensuring the stop blocks have not slipped during the rigging process?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

Do a check of the pitch trim rigging. (1) Attach an inclinometer to the trim tab. (2) Put the trim tab in the 0 degree position. (3) Manually operate the trim tab to the up and down limits. (4)  Record the limits of travel. (5) Put an observer at the right-hand access opening of the tailcone. (6) Put the electrical trim to the full nose-up position until the observer sees the clutch slip. (7) Turn the manual trim wheel nose-up  1/4 turn more while the clutch slips. (8) Make sure the swaged ball on the control cable assembly does not turn aft of the tangent point. (9) Release the trim wheel and disengage the autopilot.  Manually operate the trim to the full nose-up position.  Do a check of the trim tab position with an inclinometer.  Trim tab position that is greater than the limits of travel values recorded is an indication that the stop blocks slipped. (a) Do the trim system rigging again. (b) Make sure the stop block bolts torque is correct. (c)  Do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  If necessary, make adjustments to the swaged ball position. (a) Put the control cable assembly chain in the applicable position on the gear teeth of the actuator sprocket. NOTE:  One chain link adjustment is related to approximately 17 degrees of travel on the capstan. (b) Apply the applicable tension to the control cable and do the check of the pitch trim rigging again.  Do the procedure again for the full nose-down trim condition.

question: What are the key safety and procedural steps to properly inspect the pitch servo's cover, solenoid, clutch, and motor while preventing electrostatic damage and ensuring correct operation?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do Inspection of the Pitch Servo . (1) Remove the servo cover. CAUTION: Make sure the maintenance personnel and the table are electrically grounded.  Do disassembly or assembly of the servo at an electrostatic-safe area. (a) Put an electrical ground on the maintenance personnel and table. (b)  Remove the two screws that attach the cover to the unit. (c) Carefully remove the cover from the wiring harness. CAUTION: Do not move any wires, tie wraps or the spring clamp. The position of each is set by the manufacturer and is necessary for correct operation. (d) Put the servo on the table so the inner parts of the unit will not be damaged. (2) Do inspection of the solenoid and clutch. (a) Make sure the solenoid shaft moves freely in and out of the solenoid body. (b) Make sure there is no dirt, contamination or corrosion around the solenoid shaft. (c)  Make sure the release spring freely pulls the shaft out of the solenoid and against the stop fitting. (d) Make sure the pinion gear turns and does not touch the clutch gears. (3) Do a general inspection. (a) Examine the electrical wiring for indication of wear or damage of the insulation. (b) Examine the servo for any loose hardware or other defects. (4) Do an inspection of the pitch servo motor. (a) Put the servo in position so the baseplate is on the bottom side of the unit. (b) Hold the top section of the motor and carefully turn the motor shaft. (c)  The motor shaft must turn freely from side to side a small quantity. (5) Install the cover. (a) Carefully put the cover in position. (b) Install the screws with Loctite 222 or Loctite 242. (6) Remove the servo capstan assembly and do a check of the slip-clutch torque setting .

question: What is the procedure for adjusting the autopilot roll null to ensure the servo drive voltage is within the specified range during pre-flight testing?
answer:
CAUTION: Do not use alternative materials or substitute parts during this panel replacement. Using unapproved approved parts may lead to respiratory issues and void the warranty.

Set the Autopilot Roll Null . (1) Make sure the autopilot flight computer completes the pre-flight test. (2) Disconnect the roll servo connector from the airplane harness. (3) Apply a ground to pin K of the harness connector. (4) Connect a digital multimeter across the harness connector at pins D and L to monitor the servo drive voltage. (5) Push the autopilot AP button on the autopilot flight computer to engage it. (a)  Make sure the default ROL mode is set. NOTE:  For example, the HDG, NAV or APR modes are not engaged. (b)  Use a DMVM to measure the DC voltage across pins D and L of the roll servo harness connector. (c) Adjust the pot until a value of 0 volts, +0.020 or -0.020 volts are measured. 1  If the end of the pot movement is reached before the servo drive is nulled, disengage the autopilot, turn the pot fully to the opposite stop and then engage the autopilot. (d) The roll null adjustment range emulates a four turn pot that lets the method of the pot adjustment range to be set. NOTE:  This adjustment lets offsets be in the roll axes.  This includes the turn coordinator. (e) Continue to turn the pot to null the voltage. (6) Connect the airplane roll servo harness connector to the servo connector.
